topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, setting expectations about the complexity and importance of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundational concepts and central activation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental principles of the complement system, including its general function, nomenclature conventions, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three distinct recognition pathways that initiate complement activation and converge to achieve the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector functions of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream mechanisms through which activated complement destroys pathogens and enhances immune defense.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes associated with deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement and applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens counteract complement defenses and how evasion proteins are utilized in laboratory and clinical settings.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and preview of next session
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing by concluding the complement series and announcing the next lecture topic.
